title: Isolated service-group orchestration and graceful degradation policy
creator: Priya Nambiar
description:
Problem: Dedicated and Private customers run isolated control planes with heterogeneous capacity and SLO profiles. During upgrades, regional incidents, or noisy-tenant events we currently risk cross-service disruption if an entire instance pool is drained or if admission control is too coarse-grained. This ticket defines orchestration and policy to manage service-group level isolation, safe rolling upgrades, circuit-breakers and automated load-shedding so that affected groups degrade predictably without bringing down healthy tenants.

Scope: orchestration policies for service-groups (logical grouping of tenants/resources within a dedicated/private control plane), admission control hooks, safe KV/worker drain procedure, circuit-breaker types (soft vs hard), and integration with routing and the console for runbooks and dashboards. Excludes: underlying kernel changes, model quantization work, and hosted multi-tenant routing logic.

Goal: Provide an operational playbook + code changes that guarantee: 1) upgrades and regional failovers limit blast radius to affected service-groups, 2) automated load-shedding respects per-group SLOs and priority policies, and 3) rolling upgrades have automated rollback triggers when SLO regressions are detected.
acceptance_criteria:
1) Service-group admission controller implemented and enabled behind feature flag in dedicated/private control plane.
2) Two circuit-breaker modes implemented: 'soft' (priority-based shed) and 'hard' (immediate cut) with config per service-group.
3) KV cache and session drain procedure completes within defined grace window with no token loss for pinned sessions in 95% of test runs.
4) Automated rollback triggers based on SLO regression (error rate + p99 latency threshold) executed in staging and documented.
5) Playbook and Console runbook page created and linked; on-call runbooks produce determined follow-up actions.
6) End-to-end chaos test demonstrating regional failover with at most 1% additional customer-impacted requests for unaffected groups.
technical_notes:
Architecture decisions: 1) Implement service-group layer in control plane as lightweight namespace with its own admission quota and circuit-breaker state; reuse existing routing primitives to avoid new infra. 2) Admission controller evaluates: priority_score, group_capacity_budget, active_request_count, and recent_error_window. 3) Opt for two-tier circuit breaker to allow graceful degradation before hard cut. 4) Drain: KV cache snapshots -> migrate hot keys using hotkey-mapper -> mark sessions as draining -> redirect new requests to fallback model variant. 5) Rollback detection: streaming SLO window (30s/5m/1h) with thresholds that trigger automated canary rollback and notify console.

Implementation notes: - New API: /controlplane/v1/service_groups/{id}/admission (PATCH) to update budgets and cb policy. - DB: add service_group table with policy blob (protobuf serialized). - Sidecar changes: admission plugin in sidecar enforces circuit-breaker local decisions for fastest path. - Console: per-group dashboard and runbook link.

References: Confluence doc: https://confluence.redwood.ai/display/REL/Service+Group+Orchestration PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/controlplane/pull/6732 Dashboard prototype: https://grafana.redwood.ai/d/SG-orch/sg-orchestration
rollout_plan:
1) Stage behind feature flag in dogfood dedicated cluster (1 cluster) for 48h.
2) Canary on 10% of service-groups in one customer region for 72h with automated rollback criteria.
3) Gradual ramp to 50% of service-groups in dedicated fleets over one week, monitoring SLOs and error budgets.
4) Full enablement after 2 weeks with retrospective and postmortem.
5) Emergency off switch: feature flag + circuit-breaker global disable in Console.

Rollback criteria: p99 latency increase > 25% over baseline for 5m AND error rate > 0.5% above baseline for 5m. Manual rollback allowed by on-call lead.
testing_plan:
Unit tests for admission logic and policy parsing. Integration tests: simulated load with mixed priorities to validate soft/hard breaker behavior. Chaos tests: network partition and a noisy-tenant storm in a dedicated region to validate isolation. End-to-end: staged upgrade with canary and rollback in staging; run automated regression against SLO suites. Performance: ensure admission sidecar adds <1ms median latency to request path.

Test artifacts: Load harness run 2026-03-05: https://ci.redwood.ai/builds/sg-orch-20260305 Results summary: 95th p99 latency preserved, drain complete within 12s for typical groups.
monitoring_and_alerting:
Dashboards: SG-Orchestration Overview, Per-Service-Group SLOs, Circuit-Breaker Events.
Metrics to emit: sg.admission.rejected_count, sg.circuit_breaker.state_changes, sg.drain.duration_seconds, sg.kv_migrate.latency, sg.slo.error_rate, sg.slo.p99_latency.
Alerts: - sg.circuit_breaker.flip_rate > 5/min -> P1 on-call. - sg.drain.failure_rate > 1% -> P1. - Automated rollback executed -> notify eng-leads + SRE channel.
Logging: structured events with service_group_id, action, reason, origin-node. Audit logs surfaced to Console for Private installs.
